claims.text: The initial cast eutectic high-entropy alloy consists of alternating ductile FCC and hard B2 lamellae.
Rapid annealing followed by controlled fast cooling refines the eutectic lamellar spacing.
Rapid annealing followed by controlled fast cooling improves coherence at FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
Refining lamellar spacing and improving FCC/B2 interface coherence simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
Rapid annealing accelerates diffusion selectively at elevated temperature.
The accelerated diffusion during rapid annealing allows homogenization.
A controlled rapid quench preserves the refined microstructure formed during annealing.
Reduced lamellar spacing increases obstruction of dislocation motion.
Greater obstruction of dislocation motion increases strength.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces mitigate early crack initiation.
Mitigation of early crack initiation prevents the strength increase from significantly sacrificing ductility.
Relative to the conventional as-cast alloy, the rapidly annealed alloy will have increased yield strength.
Relative to the conventional as-cast alloy, the rapidly annealed alloy will have increased uniform elongation.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement should be observable during room-temperature mechanical testing.
Cooling rates that deviate significantly from an optimal range may fail to produce the required microstructural refinement.
Failure to achieve sufficient microstructural refinement may prevent simultaneous improvement of strength and ductility.
